newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin's doctor optimistic about full recovery.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's doctor optimistic about full recovery.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin will be able to hunt and fish in up to four weeks, travel abroad in January and play tennis next spring, chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov told Interfax news agency on Saturday.
"Boris Nikolayevich wants to be ahead of the schedule in everything and everywhere," Mironov said, praising Yeltsin's eagerness to obey doctors' instructions.
Following orders, Yeltsin lost between eight and 10 kilos (18 to 22 lb) before his quintuple heart bypass operation on November 5, Mironov said.
Yeltsin's condition was "quite satisfactory and adequately active".
Yeltsin, 65, left the Central Clinical Hospital on Friday and moved to his favourite Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow.
During a television appearance from Barvikha, Yeltsin looked much thinner than before the surgery but was speaking more clearly, firmly and with more animation.
On Saturday, the president is scheduled to meet the first foreign visitor since his operation, Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev.
